patch.value: Tokens-per-fact encoding study: measure every output encoding against an information-equivalence baseline and adopt the cheapest per surface

pm has TOON and JSON output and a default of TOON for agent loops, chosen on reasoning rather than measurement. No item owns the question of how many tokens pm spends to deliver one unit of information, which is the actual currency of an agent workspace. This item establishes the measurement and then lets it decide. Define a fact set — the specific field values an agent must receive for a given command and intent — and measure, per encoding, the tokenizer cost of delivering exactly that fact set with nothing else. Candidate encodings to measure, not to presume: TOON as it exists; JSON as it exists; a key-hoisted tabular form where repeated field names appear once per result set rather than once per row; an ordinal form where a contract-declared field order removes names entirely for known projections; and a hybrid that hoists keys only above a row-count threshold. Measure across representative result sizes, because the winner at one row is not the winner at five hundred. The deliverable is a measured table plus a per-surface default, not a universal winner.

A reproducible benchmark defines the required fact set per measured command and intent, and rejects any encoding that omits a required fact rather than scoring it as cheaper; Tokenizer cost is measured for every candidate encoding at small, medium, and large result sizes, and the results are published as a table with the measurement method; A per-surface default encoding is selected from the measurements and recorded with its rationale, including surfaces where the existing default wins; Human readability is scored as an explicit criterion, so a marginal token win cannot silently make output unreadable; The benchmark runs in CI as a regression gate so an encoding change that raises tokens-per-fact fails; Any new default encoding is reachable through the uniform format-flag grammar and every prior spelling keeps working
The default encoding of every read surface is the measured cheapest encoding that preserves the required facts
Encoding overhead is paid on every single command an agent runs; a percentage saved here compounds across every agent, every session, and every workspace forever
May change default output encodings on read surfaces; must land behind the uniform output contract so the change is one coordinated decision rather than per-command drift
Agents spend measurably fewer tokens per unit of delivered context, with the tradeoff recorded rather than assumed
Encoding defaults get frozen by the v1.0 grammar and output-contract work, so measuring after the freeze is measuring too late

message: File the tokens-per-fact measurement that should decide encoding defaults before the grammar freeze

GitHub report #1373: Agent UX: pm next default output is 9 KB / 315 lines for 11 rows because ready/blocked rows are expanded, not tabular
Source: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1373
Created: 2026-10-02T18:24:26Z; updated: 2026-10-02T18:24:26Z.
The report uses published pm 2026.10.2. Its byte/line measurements and proposals are source observations, not measured tokenizer results or implemented acceptance. Revalidate in controlled fixtures before changing the SDK projection and thin CLI adapters. Preserve required facts, rank/blocker semantics, complete restoration paths and JSON compatibility.

## Summary
`pm next` is the command an agent runs most often to decide what to do, yet its default output is the largest of the everyday read commands. On a real 928-item tracker (pm 2026.10.2, default `--limit 5`):

| command | bytes | lines |
|---|---|---|
| `pm next` | 8,976 | 315 |
| `pm context --limit 10` | 6,249 | 212 |
| `pm list-open --limit 20` | 3,360 | 51 |
| `pm get <id>` | 2,082 | 54 |

`pm next` returns at most 11 rows (1 recommended + 5 ready + 5 blocked) but spends ~28 lines per row, while `list-open` returns 20 rows in 51 lines.

## Cause
Each ready/blocked row is rendered as an expanded TOON object because it carries a `tags` array (one line per tag) plus nested `blockers[n]{...}`. Arrays inside rows prevent TOON from using its tabular form, so every field becomes its own line:

```
ready:
  - id: "pm-cli-website-204t"
    title: "Specify pm-rust: ..."
    type: "Feature"
    status: "in_progress"
    priority: 1
    tags:
      - "agents"
      - "architecture"
      ... (7 tag lines)
    updated_at: "..."
    open_blocker_count: 0
    rank: 2
```

## Proposal
Make the default projection of `ready` and `blocked` tabular, like `list-open` already is:

```
ready[5]{rank,id,priority,status,type,title,parent,open_blocker_count}:
  2,pm-cli-website-204t,1,in_progress,Feature,"Specify pm-rust: ...",,0
blocked[5]{rank,id,priority,status,title,blocked_by}:
  1,pm-cli-website-hua9,1,open,"Record and publish ...",pm-cli-website-j4w8
```

- Keep `recommended` as the single expanded object, including `reasons` and tags; it is the row an agent acts on.
- Omit `tags` and `updated_at` from ready/blocked rows by default (or join tags into one string) and add an `omission_receipt` with `--full` / `--fields tags` as the restore path, matching `pm get`.
- Flatten `blockers[n]{id,title,status}` to a `blocked_by` id list in the brief view.

Measured on the same tracker, this would cut `pm next` from ~315 to roughly 30 lines, with no loss of the information an agent needs to pick the next item.

Related, broader: #1363 (lightweight defaults). This issue is the concrete, measurable `pm next` slice.

GitHub report #1374: Agent UX: pm get prints notes_count and tests_count next to collection_counts, which already carries both
Source: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1374
Created: 2026-10-02T18:24:38Z; updated: 2026-10-02T18:24:38Z.
The report uses published pm 2026.10.2. Its byte/line measurements and proposals are source observations, not measured tokenizer results or implemented acceptance. Revalidate in controlled fixtures before changing the SDK projection and thin CLI adapters. Preserve required facts, rank/blocker semantics, complete restoration paths and JSON compatibility.

## Summary
`pm get <id>` (2026.10.2, default TOON) prints two counters twice:

```
  notes_count: 6
  tests_count: 0
  collection_counts:
    comments: 1
    notes: 6
    learnings: 0
    files: 0
    tests: 0
    docs: 6
    reminders: 0
    events: 0
```

`notes_count` duplicates `collection_counts.notes` and `tests_count` duplicates `collection_counts.tests`. Zero-valued collection counters (`learnings: 0`, `files: 0`, `reminders: 0`, `events: 0`) also cost a line each on every `get`, and `pm get` is the most frequent per-item read an agent makes.

## Proposal
- Drop `notes_count` and `tests_count` from the default item projection (keep them under `--full`/`--json` for compatibility, or deprecate there too).
- Print `collection_counts` as one inline object of the non-zero counters, e.g. `collection_counts: {comments: 1, notes: 6, docs: 6}`, and state in the existing `omission_receipt` that zero counters were omitted.

Small per call (about 6 of 54 lines here), but it applies to every `pm get`. Related: #1363 (lightweight defaults).
